stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: A sudden burst of 200 analytical tasks saturates all worker threads. Fast, mission- critical user read requests queue behind 5- second exports, blowing past client SLAs and causing outage alerts.
Breakdown Chain: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.

tradeOffs: Architectural Invariant: "Workloads with disparate latency profiles must never share a single execution queue; enforce physical bulkhead pool isolation."

approachSteps: 1. Track real-time latency gradients and inflight concurrency.
2. Reject excess traffic at the ingress boundary within <0.1ms.
3. Monitor P99 latency and verify autonomous recovery when downstream pressure subsides.
